mainTopic: The question of אחאי בריבי about a pig-like animal nursing from a ewe (תיקו), and clearing hair before slaughtering a בכור, including whether it is allowed on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens with the question of אחאי בריבי: what is the law if a pig-like animal is seen trailing after a ewe to nurse? The גמרא explains that he is really asking two questions. One is about בכורה according to the רבנן. The other is about eating the animal according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Both depend on whether a mother animal nurses young of another species out of mercy, and the question ends with תיקו. Next comes a new משנה. In it, רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows a person slaughtering a בכור to clear the neck hair with a cleaver, as long as the hair stays in place, and to pluck hair to check a מום. רב rules like רבי יוסי בן המשולם. Students ask רב הונא whether the same is allowed for an ordinary animal on יום טוב. After confirming רב's ruling through רב חננאל, רב הונא rules that it is permitted. A second report in רב's name, from רב חנניה בר שלמיא, begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A pig-like animal trailing after a ewe
steps.stepSummary: אחאי בריבי asks what the law is when someone sees a pig-looking animal following a ewe to nurse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחאי בריבי asked: If someone saw a pig-like animal trailing after a ewe, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked. Someone saw a pig-looking young animal following a ewe as if it were her baby, and אחאי בריבי wants to know the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is 'כרוך אחר' another animal is following it to nurse. That suggests the ewe may be its mother. The problem is that this baby looks like a pig, not like a sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor ('the distinguished one')
Pig (here: an animal that looks like a pig)
Trailing after, following closely (as a nursing baby does)

phrases.english: Aḥai the Distinguished asked:
phrases.notes: The verb 'asked' (בעי) comes just before this line, at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: If one saw a pig-like animal trailing after a ewe,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה חֲזִיר שֶׁכָּרוּךְ אַחַר רָחֵל, מַהוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law when a pig-like animal follows a ewe to nurse?

steps.title: Why ask about a pig rather than a lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the question really is. If it were only about the בכורה dispute between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן, a normal lamb would have been the simpler case to ask about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he asking? If you say he is asking about the firstborn status, meaning he wants to know whether the law follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן, then let him ask about a lamb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. If the issue were simply which side of the known dispute we follow, why bring a strange pig-like animal into it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier dispute about whether a ewe seen nursing a baby is assumed to be its mother, which would exempt her later offspring from בכורה. A plain question about that dispute would be asked with an ordinary lamb. Choosing the pig-like case must mean there is a different point being asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn status (whether the ewe's next offspring is a בכור)

phrases.english: What is he asking about?
If we say it is regarding firstborn status,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ אִי הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: and he is asking whether the law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
or whether the law follows the Rabbis,
then let him ask about a lamb!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the point of the step 1 question is
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of a pig-like animal in the question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the question were only which opinion we follow, the pig detail adds nothing. An ordinary lamb would be the natural case to ask about.

steps.title: Two separate questions, one for each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two questions. One is about בכורה, asked according to the רבנן. The other is about eating the animal, asked according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he asked, it was about firstborn status according to the רבנן, and about eating according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that he is not asking which opinion is right. He is asking a new question within each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pig detail matters for both questions. For the רבנן, it raises a new בכורה question. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, it raises a new question about whether the animal may be eaten. The next two steps explain each question.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating (whether the animal is permitted as food)

phrases.english: When he asked,
it was regarding firstborn status, according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: לַאֲכִילָה וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: and regarding eating, according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, לִבְכוֹרָה וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the question is not which opinion is correct but a new question within each opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was simply whether we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two questions: בכורה according to the רבנן, and eating according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The בכורה question according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that an animal may nurse young out of mercy. The question is whether that mercy extends to young of another species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding firstborn status: even according to the רבנן, who say an animal shows mercy, perhaps it shows mercy only to its own species and not to another species. Or perhaps it shows mercy even to another species?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first question. According to the רבנן, can a ewe nurse a baby of a different kind just out of mercy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say nursing does not prove motherhood, because an animal may kindly nurse another's young. If that kindness applies only to her own species, then a ewe nursing a pig-like baby must be its real mother. She has already given birth, so her next offspring is exempt from בכורה. If her kindness extends to other species too, nursing proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Shows mercy (nurses young that may not be her own)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'mercy' does not mean the law is being lenient. It means the mother animal kindly nurses a baby that may not be hers. That is why nursing alone may not prove she is the mother.

phrases.english: Regarding firstborn status, even according to the Rabbis, who say an animal shows mercy,
perhaps it shows mercy only to one of its own species,
but to one not of its species, it does not;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא דְּלָא מִינַהּ נָמֵי מְרַחֲמָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps it also shows mercy to one not of its species?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the step 3 answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an animal's mercy (nursing young that are not hers) extend to young of a different species?

steps.title: The eating question according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that a mother who has given birth may nurse others out of mercy. The question is whether she does so for another species too. The answer decides whether the pig-like animal is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding eating: even according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if you say he holds that a mother who has given birth shows mercy, perhaps that is only to her own species and not to another species. Or perhaps she shows mercy even to another species?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second question. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, is the pig-like animal really the ewe's baby, which would make it permitted to eat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mother nurses only her own species, then a ewe nursing this pig-like animal shows it is her baby. Something born from a kosher ewe is permitted to eat, even if it looks like a pig. If she might nurse another species out of mercy, the animal may really be a pig and is forbidden to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that / if you say
An animal that has given birth

phrases.aramaic: לַאֲכִילָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל —
phrases.english: Regarding eating, even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
if you say he holds that
a mother who gave birth shows mercy to her own species,
but to one not of her species, she does not;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: דְּלָאו מִינַהּ נָמֵי מְרַחֲמָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps she also shows mercy to one not of her species?

steps.triggerLanguage: לַאֲכִילָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the step 3 answer, using the same 'own species' idea as step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a mother who has given birth nurse young of another species out of mercy? The answer decides whether the pig-like animal is kosher.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stays open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer the question of אחאי בריבי, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both parts, בכורה according to the רבנן and eating according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, remain unresolved. We do not know whether a mother's mercy extends to another species.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The question of אחאי בריבי has two parts: בכורה according to the רבנן, and eating according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Both depend on whether a mother animal nurses young of another species out of mercy. The answer is תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes both questions from steps 4 and 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is unresolved whether an animal's mercy extends to another species. So both the בכורה question and the eating question remain in doubt.

steps.title: New משנה: Clearing hair before slaughtering a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows a person slaughtering a בכור to clear hair from the neck with a cleaver. The pulled hair must stay in its place. He also allows plucking hair so a blemish can be examined.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: Someone who slaughters a בכור makes room with a cleaver on this side and that side, and pulls out the hair. But he must not move the hair from its place. He may also pull out hair to see where a blemish is.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It teaches how to prepare a בכור's neck for שחיטה without breaking the rule against shearing a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids shearing a בכור. Clearing the wool with a cleaver pulls out some hair, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows it. The pulled hair must stay mixed in with the rest, so it does not look like shearing. Plucking hair to check a מום is allowed for the same kind of reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here introducing a new one)
A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy and may not be sheared
Plucks or pulls out by the root
A blemish; a בכור with a blemish may be slaughtered outside the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. The previous discussion about nursing animals ended with תיקו. Do not try to connect this משנה to it.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
One who slaughters the firstborn,
makes space with a cleaver from here and from there,
phrases.notes: He clears the wool on both sides of the neck so he can cut properly.

phrases.english: and he plucks out the hair,
provided that he does not move it from its place;
phrases.notes: The pulled hair stays mixed in, so it does not look like shearing.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תּוֹלֵשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר לִרְאוֹת מְקוֹם מוּם.
phrases.english: and likewise he plucks the hair to see the place of a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the previous תיקו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When slaughtering a בכור, one may clear the hair with a cleaver as long as the hair is not moved from its place. One may also pluck hair to examine a blemish.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי בן המשולם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by giving the final הלכה on this משנה: we follow רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling becomes the base for the next question. Students will ask what רב's ruling teaches about a similar case on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
A leading early אמורא in Babylonia

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.

steps.title: The question about יום טוב, first possibility: plucking is not shearing
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב הונא whether one may do the same thing to an ordinary animal on יום טוב. Maybe רבי יוסי בן המשולם allowed it only because plucking is not shearing. If so, plucking would still be forbidden on יום טוב, because it counts as uprooting something from where it grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב הונא: What about the same case on יום טוב? Maybe רבי יוסי בן המשולם's reason is that he holds plucking is not the same as shearing. If so, on יום טוב it is forbidden, because it counts as uprooting something from where it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: Students ask רב הונא a new question: does the בכור rule also apply to slaughtering a regular animal on יום טוב? They begin by laying out the first side of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a בכור, the only problem is shearing. If plucking is not shearing, there is no problem with a בכור. But יום טוב has a different forbidden labor, עוקר דבר מגידולו. Plucking clearly falls under that labor, so on this reading it would be forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked of him (a formal question)
A Festival day, when certain labors are forbidden
Uprooting something from where it grows, a forbidden labor

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two prohibitions. For a בכור the concern is shearing. On יום טוב the concern is uprooting from where it grows. Plucking can escape the first and still fall under the second.

phrases.english: They asked of Rav Huna:
What is the parallel case on a Festival?
phrases.notes: Clearing hair from an ordinary animal's neck in order to slaughter it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Is the reason of Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר תּוֹלֵשׁ לָאו הַיְינוּ גּוֹזֵז,
phrases.english: because he holds that plucking is not the same as shearing,
and on a Festival it is forbidden,
since it is uprooting an item from its place of growth?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב הוּנָא: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's ruling to ask about a related case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may pluck hair from an ordinary animal before slaughtering it on יום טוב. This depends on the reasoning behind רבי יוסי בן המשולם's ruling.

steps.title: Second possibility: plucking is shearing, but it is unintended
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי יוסי בן המשולם does hold that plucking counts as shearing. He allows it only because it is a דבר שאין מתכוין. If so, it would also be allowed on יום טוב, since a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe in general רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds that plucking is shearing. The reason he allows it is that it is an unintended result. On יום טוב, an unintended result is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The students give the other side of their doubt. Under this side, the יום טוב case would be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the permission does not come from defining plucking as something other than shearing. It comes from intention: the person only wants to make room for the knife, not to pull out hair. That reason, דבר שאין מתכוין, works on יום טוב too, so this reading would permit it there.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
An unintended act: doing something permitted that might accidentally cause a forbidden result

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בְּעָלְמָא סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
phrases.english: Or perhaps, in general, Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam holds
that plucking is the same as shearing,
and this is the reason that he permits it:
because it is an unintended act,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיוֹם טוֹב דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין מוּתָּר?
phrases.english: and on a Festival an unintended act is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא בְּעָלְמָא סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the same question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the permission is based on דבר שאין מתכוין, which would allow the same act on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב הונא sends them to confirm רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells the students to ask רב חננאל whether רב really ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם. If he did, רב הונא will answer their question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go ask רב חננאל. If he says that רב ruled the הלכה is like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, I will resolve it for you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup step. רב הונא does not answer yet. He first wants to be sure of רב's exact ruling, because his answer depends on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer depends on the confirmed ruling of רב. So before answering, he checks with רב חננאל, a student of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of רב who reported his teachings
I will resolve it for you

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל,
phrases.english: He said to them: Go ask Rav Ḥananel;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: if he says that the halakha is like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,
I will resolve it for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares the answer by first verifying רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא will answer only after confirming that רב ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם.

steps.title: רב חננאל confirms רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The students go to רב חננאל. He confirms that רב said the הלכה is like רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and asked him. He said to them: This is what רב said: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The students check with רב חננאל, and he confirms the report: רב did rule like רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition רב הונא set is now met. רב's ruling is confirmed, so רב הונא can give his answer.

phrases.english: They went and asked him;
he said to them: This is what Rav says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב did rule that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.

steps.title: רב הונא rules: on יום טוב it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The students return to רב הונא. He rules that plucking hair to prepare an animal for שחיטה is permitted on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רב הונא. He said to them: In the parallel case on יום טוב, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רב's ruling is confirmed, רב הונא answers the original question: clearing the hair before slaughtering on יום טוב is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitting it on יום טוב fits the second side of the question in step 10. On that side, the reason is דבר שאין מתכוין, and that reason works on יום טוב too.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, building on רב's ruling, a person may clear hair from an animal's neck before slaughtering it on יום טוב, just as with a בכור.

phrases.english: They came before Rav Huna;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: he said to them: The parallel case on a Festival is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the promised answer after the confirmation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plucking hair to prepare an animal for שחיטה on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: A second report in רב's name begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another report in רב's name, from רב חנניה בר שלמיא, about the same יום טוב case. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב חנניה בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: In the parallel case on יום טוב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a second source on the same question. This line is a setup; the actual ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase איתמר נמי usually brings a separate tradition that backs up what was just said. Here it introduces a direct statement from רב about the יום טוב case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces a supporting tradition)
A student who reports teachings of רב
